Mctt.Core.Syntactic.System.Definitions

The Syntactic Judgments

Substitution is a meta-level operation rather than a syntactic constructor, so:
  • there is no wf_exp_sub rule and there are no _sub computation rules; how a substitution distributes over each term former, how substitutions compose and what the identity does are theorems about exp_sub, proved in Core.Syntactic.Substitution and used by rewrite;
  • the four judgments about terms (context well-formedness, typing, term equality and subtyping) mention no substitution judgment, and are mutually defined with the six about units, extensions, module expressions and the global context;
  • weakening and substitution typing are derived judgments: statements that an operation maps every binding of one context to something of the right type in the other. Their closure properties (identity, extension, lifting, composition) are lemmas, in Core.Syntactic.System.Structural.
One rule is stated more generally than in the paper:
  • wf_subtyp_pi checks the codomains in Γ ▹ A' rather than Γ ▹ A. The two are interderivable given Γ ⊢ A ≈ A' : Typeω@i and context conversion, and Γ ▹ A' is what the soundness proof wants.
Every judgment reads the two global components a global resolves in: the filed units Θ and the definition stack Ξ, as in Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A. They are indices, not parameters: no rule about terms changes them, but a filed unit is checked against the units before it and a stack frame against the frames outside it, so ⊢ᵍ Θ ⍮ Ξ is an induction that varies them, as ⊢ Γ varies Γ.

From Stdlib Require Import Lia List Classes.RelationClasses Setoid Morphisms.

Θ at next level, as Γ of the short form ⊢ Γ (Fixed.v), so that the two share their prefix and parse together.

Generalizable All Variables.

Context Lookup

A lookup carries the weakenings that separate the binding from the top of the context, so Var below needs no shifting of its own. The shift here is the weakening ↑, not the substitution Wk: everything that has to move a looked-up type past a lifted operation does so with exp_wk_shift_wk_q or exp_wk_shift_sub_q, both of which are stated for ↑.

Inductive ctx_lookup : nat -> typ -> ctx -> Prop :=
  
The innermost entry, an assumption: its type, weakened past it
  | here : `(Γ ▹{κ} A ∋ #0 : A[↑]ʷ)
  
The innermost entry, a definition: its type, weakened past it
  | here_def : `(Γ ▸ A ≔ M ∋ #0 : A[↑]ʷ)
  
The innermost entry, a definition with a module part: the type of its term part, weakened past it
  | here_dm : `(Γ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ U ∋ #0 : A[↑]ʷ)
  
An entry under one more entry: its type, weakened past that one too
  | there : `(Γ ∋ #n : A -> e :: Γ ∋ #(S n) : A[↑]ʷ)
where "Γ ∋ '#' x : A" := (ctx_lookup x A Γ) : type_scope.

The body of a definition entry, weakened to the use site like its type.
Inductive ctx_lookup_def : nat -> typ -> exp -> ctx -> Prop :=
  
The innermost entry, a definition: its body and its type, weakened past it
  | def_here : `(Γ ▸ A ≔ M ∋ #0 ≔ M[↑]ʷ : A[↑]ʷ)
  
The innermost entry, a definition with a module part: the body and the type of its term part, weakened past it
  | def_here_dm : `(Γ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ U ∋ #0 ≔ M[↑]ʷ : A[↑]ʷ)
  
A definition under one more entry: its body and type, weakened past that one too
  | def_there : `(Γ ∋ #n ≔ M : A -> e :: Γ ∋ #(S n) ≔ M[↑]ʷ : A[↑]ʷ)
where "Γ ∋ '#' x ≔ M : A" := (ctx_lookup_def x A M Γ) : type_scope.

Shapes of Units

A telescope of parameters has assumptions only (all_assumptions, with the member types in Members).
Two bodies compared entry by entry: the same names and kinds in the same order, the same privacy, and transparent definitions with a body, of the same sort; and local opens at the same places, with the same items.
Definition entry_shape (E E' : gentry) : Prop :=
  match E, E' with
  | ge_def b pv κ _ (Some _), ge_def b' pv' κ' _ (Some _) => b = true /\ b' = true /\ pv = pv' /\ κ = κ'
  | ge_mod pv _, ge_mod pv' _ => pv = pv'
  | ge_def_mod pv _ _ _, ge_def_mod pv' _ _ _ => pv = pv'
  | _, _ => False
  end.

Fixpoint body_shape (Φ Φ' : gmod) : Prop :=
  match Φ, Φ' with
  | gm_nil, gm_nil => True
  | gm_ext Φ x E, gm_ext Φ' x' E' => body_shape Φ Φ' /\ x = x' /\ entry_shape E E'
  (* the stored definitions too, as the expansions are (body_xp) *)
  | gm_open Φ _ its Φg, gm_open Φ' _ its' Φg' => body_shape Φ Φ' /\ its = its' /\ body_shape Φg Φg'
  | _, _ => False
  end.

The sorts of the types: a type is in a large universe, is a proposition, in Prop, or is a type of levels, in LevelSort. type_sort S says that S is one of them, so Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : S with type_sort S says that A is a type. Neither a proposition nor a type of levels is in a universe (Prop and LevelSort sit beside the cumulative hierarchy), so a rule that takes a type of any sort takes its sort as a premise.
Inductive type_sort : exp -> Prop :=
A large universe: the types of the universes
| type_sort_universe : forall i, type_sort (Typeω@i)
Prop: the propositions
| type_sort_prop : type_sort Propₘ
LevelSort: the types of levels, and the Πs between them
| type_sort_level : type_sort LevelSort.

sort_kind S κ: the types of the sort S are of the kind κ — a large universe's of ak_relevant, Prop's of ak_propositional, LevelSort's of ak_level. A context entry, a binder and a definition carry the kind of their type's sort.
Inductive sort_kind : exp -> abs_kind -> Prop :=
A large universe
| sort_kind_universe : forall i, sort_kind (Typeω@i) ak_relevant
Prop
| sort_kind_prop : sort_kind Propₘ ak_propositional
LevelSort
| sort_kind_level : sort_kind LevelSort ak_level.

The sort of the kind κ next to the universe U: U itself for ak_relevant, Prop and LevelSort for the others.
Definition abs_kind_sort (κ : abs_kind) (U : exp) : exp :=
  match κ with ak_relevant => U | ak_propositional => Propₘ | ak_level => LevelSort end.

The sort at a kind, moved: Prop and LevelSort stay.
Lemma abs_kind_sort_sub : forall κ S σ, (abs_kind_sort κ S)[σ] = abs_kind_sort κ S[σ].
Proof. intros [] *; reflexivity. Qed.

Lemma abs_kind_sort_wk : forall κ S φ, (abs_kind_sort κ S)[φ]ʷ = abs_kind_sort κ S[φ]ʷ.
Proof. intros [] *; reflexivity. Qed.

Next to a large universe, it is the sort of its kind.
Lemma sort_kind_abs_kind_sort : forall κ i, sort_kind (abs_kind_sort κ Typeω@i) κ.
Proof. intros [] *; constructor. Qed.

A sort of a kind is a type sort.
Lemma sort_kind_type_sort : forall S κ, sort_kind S κ -> type_sort S.
Proof. intros * []; constructor. Qed.

A sort of a kind is the sort of the kind next to a large universe.
Lemma sort_kind_abs_kind_sort_inv : forall S κ, sort_kind S κ -> exists i, S = abs_kind_sort κ Typeω@i.
Proof. intros * []; [ eexists; reflexivity | exists 0; reflexivity | exists 0; reflexivity ]. Qed.

It is a type sort when S is.
Lemma type_sort_abs_kind : forall κ S, type_sort S -> type_sort (abs_kind_sort κ S).
Proof. intros [] * HS; [ exact HS | constructor | constructor ]. Qed.

#[export]
Hint Resolve type_sort_abs_kind sort_kind_abs_kind_sort sort_kind_type_sort : mctt.

pi_kinds κd κc: the kinds of the domain and of the codomain of a Π. A Π into a type of a universe or into a proposition may be out of a domain of any kind; a Π into a type of levels only out of a type of levels, so that a level is built only from levels: λ (n : ℕ) → 0l has no type.
Inductive pi_kinds : abs_kind -> abs_kind -> Prop :=
A type of functions
| pi_kinds_relevant : forall κd, pi_kinds κd ak_relevant
A universal proposition
| pi_kinds_prop : forall κd, pi_kinds κd ak_propositional
A type of levels, out of a type of levels
| pi_kinds_level : pi_kinds ak_level ak_level.

A motive's kind: a type of a universe or a proposition, never a type of levels (no level is computed from an eliminator).
Inductive motive_kind : abs_kind -> Prop :=
Into a universe
| motive_kind_relevant : motive_kind ak_relevant
Into Prop
| motive_kind_prop : motive_kind ak_propositional.

A constructor argument's kind: in the group's universe or a proposition, never a type of levels.
Inductive carg_kind : abs_kind -> Prop :=
In the group's universe
| carg_kind_relevant : carg_kind ak_relevant
A proposition
| carg_kind_prop : carg_kind ak_propositional.

A record field's kind: in the record's universe or a proposition, never a type of levels.
Inductive field_kind : abs_kind -> Prop :=
In the record's universe
| field_kind_relevant : field_kind ak_relevant
A proposition
| field_kind_prop : field_kind ak_propositional.

level_sorted_parameters Δ: every assumption of the telescope Δ is of the kind of levels (ak_level), so a type of levels in a well-formed context. A definition whose type is a type of levels is only allowed over such parameters (wf_gentry_def): in module N (n : ℕ) where def v : Level, v would be a level computed from the number n, and is rejected. The kind is read off the entry: a type of levels and a type of a universe are told apart by it, not by typing.
Definition level_sorted_parameters (Δ : ctx) : Prop :=
  forall Δ1 κ T Δ2, Δ = Δ1 ++ ce_ass κ T :: Δ2 -> κ = ak_level.

desc_reads_frame Ξ R: the module part of the description R is stored at an open frame of Ξ: a unit, a module, the module of an inductive member or of a record type, still being defined.
Definition desc_reads_frame (Ξ : gstack) (R : mdesc) : Prop :=
  exists Θ' p T Φ Ns, mdesc_mod R = Some (mdesc_closed Θ' p T Φ Ns) /\ gc_frame Ξ p <> None.

frame_free_target Θ Ξ Γ E: what the module expression E denotes in Γ is no open frame. An alias, a definition with a module part and an open never name a module before it is filed, so that no filed module reads itself: in record P : Type@1 where a : Type@0 with module S ≔ P end the alias S would make P.S.S… read P forever, and is rejected. Selecting a finished entry through an open frame is allowed: module B ≔ A, A an earlier module of the same unit, denotes A's own description. It is stated by the description E denotes, which is unique (mdenote is functional), so that it moves as E does.
Definition frame_free_target (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (Γ : ctx) (E : modexp) : Prop :=
  exists R, mdenote Θ Ξ Γ E R /\ ~ desc_reads_frame Ξ R.

The sorts of the types of an evaluated kind (evaluated_kind: no proposition), which a definition or a codomain may have: a large universe, or LevelSort.
Inductive evaluated_sort : exp -> Prop :=
A large universe
| evaluated_sort_universe : forall i, evaluated_sort (Typeω@i)
The types of levels
| evaluated_sort_level : evaluated_sort LevelSort.

parameter_sort l S: a parameter of a unit, a frame or a declaration may be a type of the sort S, the universe at l or LevelSort. The rules give every parameter its sort by its position from the outside (param_sorts (List.length Δ2) for the parameter T of Δ1 ++ ce_ass κ T :: Δ2).
Inductive parameter_sort (l : nat) : exp -> Prop :=
A type of the universe at l
| parameter_sort_universe : parameter_sort l (Typeω@l)
A type of levels
| parameter_sort_level : parameter_sort l LevelSort.

level_closed_sort Sc Sr: a former whose result is of the sort Sr may take a component of the sort Sc. A result of a type of levels is built only from levels (the 𝕃 invariant): its components are of LevelSort. A result in a universe or in Prop takes components of any sort. λ (n : ℕ) → 0l, let n : ℕ ≔ 5 in 0l and efq h return Level@0 have no type.
Inductive level_closed_sort : exp -> exp -> Prop :=
A result in a large universe, from components of any sort
| level_closed_universe : forall Sc i, level_closed_sort Sc (Typeω@i)
A proposition, from components of any sort
| level_closed_prop : forall Sc, level_closed_sort Sc Propₘ
A level, from levels
| level_closed_level : level_closed_sort LevelSort LevelSort.

The component sort a module counts as, for a former that binds one (ℓₘ): never a type of levels, so that a local module is never at a body of a type of levels.
Inductive module_body_sort : exp -> Prop :=
A body in a large universe
| module_body_universe : forall i, module_body_sort (Typeω@i)
A proposition
| module_body_prop : module_body_sort Propₘ.

A rank rk of the members of a group D: 0 at a declared member, and below a view's at every member the view nests through in any block the eliminator at the view reads (one per member i' of the container's group, the block of the member v the view takes it to). The readback of a stuck eliminator at a view reads its branches with the eliminator at those members applied to fresh variables; the rank makes that recursion well founded.
Record view_rank_ok (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (D : ind_decl) (rk : nat -> nat) : Prop := mk_view_rank_ok
  {
A declared member has rank 0
    view_rank_ok_decl : forall k Mk pm, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> im_head Mk = mh_decl pm -> rk k = 0
    
A view's rank is above that of every member it nests through, in every block the eliminator at the view reads: by a whole argument or along a leaf path of an argument recursive in both
  ; view_rank_ok_nest : forall k Mk qc k' Is vm D' i' Mi' v Mv c gs' gs, ind_member D k = Some Mk ->
      im_head Mk = mh_view qc k' Is vm -> ind_lookup Θ Ξ qc = Some D' -> ind_member D' i' = Some Mi' ->
      List.nth_error vm i' = Some v -> ind_member D v = Some Mv -> ind_con Mi' c = Some gs' -> ind_con Mv c = Some gs ->
      cargs_nest_ok D D' rk (rk k) gs' gs
    
A record view's rank is above that of every member its recursive fields end in, at each of its constructors (it has one, rview_struct_con; the rank does not rely on that, as the check rank_check reads them all)
  ; view_rank_ok_rview : forall k Mk qr Is fl c gs gs1 t gs2, ind_member D k = Some Mk ->
      im_head Mk = mh_record qr Is fl -> List.In (c, gs) (im_cons Mk) -> gs = gs1 ++ ca_rec t :: gs2 ->
      rk (ptyp_mem t) < rk k }.

A record view's head mh_record qr Is fl names the record R filed at qr, at as many arguments as it has parameters, its fields as R's.
Record rview_record_facts (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (R : record_decl) (qr : qname) (Is : list exp) (fl : list String.string) : Prop :=
  mk_rview_record_facts
  {
R is the record filed at qr
    rview_record_lookup : record_lookup Θ Ξ qr = Some R
    
The fields are named as R's, in order
  ; rview_record_names : fl = List.map fst (record_fields R)
    
There are as many arguments as R has parameters
  ; rview_record_count : List.length Is = List.length (record_params R)
    
R's parameters are assumptions
  ; rview_record_ass : all_assumptions (record_params R)
    
The fields have distinct names, so a leaf path's projection names one field (leaf_in)
  ; rview_record_nodup : List.NoDup fl }.

The facts about the record views of a group D that involve no judgment: each is a record's at its instance (rview_record_facts), with no non-uniform parameters, its one constructor rview_con taking its fields in order, at their sorts; the record views come last (rview_suffix_ok) and their fields end only in record views before them (rview_order_ok).
Record rview_struct_ok (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (D : ind_decl) : Prop := mk_rview_struct_ok
  {
A record view is a filed record at as many arguments as it has parameters, its fields named as its head names them
    rview_struct_record : forall k Mk qr Is fl, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> im_head Mk = mh_record qr Is fl ->
      exists R, rview_record_facts Θ Ξ R qr Is fl
    
It has no non-uniform parameters
  ; rview_struct_nparams : forall k Mk qr Is fl, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> im_head Mk = mh_record qr Is fl ->
      im_nparams Mk = nil
    
Its one constructor is rview_con, of one argument per field
  ; rview_struct_con : forall k Mk qr Is fl, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> im_head Mk = mh_record qr Is fl ->
      exists gs, im_cons Mk = (rview_con, gs) :: nil /\ List.length gs = List.length fl
    
Its constructor's arguments are of the record's fields' sorts, so that the constructor and the tuple of its fields take them alike
  ; rview_struct_kinds : forall k Mk qr Is fl R gs, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> im_head Mk = mh_record qr Is fl ->
      record_lookup Θ Ξ qr = Some R -> im_cons Mk = (rview_con, gs) :: nil ->
      cargs_kinds gs = record_field_kinds R
    
The record views come last
  ; rview_struct_suffix : rview_suffix_ok D
    
Their fields end only in record views before them
  ; rview_struct_order : rview_order_ok D }.

vmv is the map of the view of D that a view with map vm takes the container's member M to: vm itself at a declared M; at a view M with map vm'', vm'' followed by vm, each of its members one vm maps. A record view is taken to a record view, never to a view.
Definition view_map_at (vm : list nat) (M : imember) (vmv : list nat) : Prop :=
  match im_head M with
  | mh_decl _ => vmv = vm
  | mh_view _ _ _ vm'' => List.map (List.nth_error vm) vm'' = List.map Some vmv
  | mh_record _ _ _ => False
  end.

The views of a group agree on their maps: of a view k with map vm and a member i' of its container, the member v of D vm takes i' to is a view of map view_map_at vm Mi'. The core command collects one view per instance, with its siblings, so the groups it builds have it; the eliminator at a view and the one at its container read a neutral alike only with it.
Definition view_maps_coherent (Θ : gdeps) (Ξ : gstack) (D : ind_decl) : Prop :=
  forall k Mk qc k' Is vm D' i' Mi' v Mv qv kv Iv vmv,
    ind_member D k = Some Mk -> im_head Mk = mh_view qc k' Is vm ->
    ind_lookup Θ Ξ qc = Some D' -> ind_member D' i' = Some Mi' ->
    List.nth_error vm i' = Some v -> ind_member D v = Some Mv -> im_head Mv = mh_view qv kv Iv vmv ->
    view_map_at vm Mi' vmv.

The Mutually Defined Judgments

Four about terms, three about units, extensions and module expressions, and three about the global context. All ten are one Inductive … with …: an entry's type and body are checked by the term judgments, so presupposition has to be proved for all of them at once.

Inductive wf_ctx : gdeps -> gstack -> ctx -> Prop :=
The base case carries what the judgment is relative to, as wf_gmod_nil and wf_gstack_nil do; wf_ctx_extend then needs no context premise of its own, since typing its head presupposes one. This is the edge that makes the block genuinely mutual in both directions: a term appeals to ⊢ᵍ, and ⊢ᵍ is checked by the term judgments.
| wf_ctx_empty :
  `( ⊢ᵍ Θ ⍮ Ξ ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ⋅ )
An assumption, at the kind of its type's sort
| wf_ctx_extend :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     sort_kind Srt κ ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κ} A )
| wf_ctx_extend_def :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ A ≔ M )
A module slot holds a well-formed unit.
| wf_ctx_extend_mod :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵘ U ≈ U ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹ₘ U )
A definition with a module part: a definition and a module slot. Its type is a type of a universe: what has a module part is never a proof. Its module part is an alias under no parameters: a local alias is never parameterized, and names no module still being defined (wf_unit_eq_alias).
| wf_ctx_extend_dm :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵘ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ≈ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) )
where "⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ" := (wf_ctx Θ Ξ Γ) : type_scope

with wf_exp : gdeps -> gstack -> ctx -> typ -> exp -> Prop :=
A large universe is in the next one.
| wf_typ :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Typeω@i : Typeω@(S i) )
A small universe at a level is in the small universe at the next one. The level is an arbitrary term, so a universe may be indexed by a variable.
| wf_univ :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Type⟨M⟩ : Type⟨succl M⟩ )
Every type of levels is of the sort of the types of levels, and in no universe.
| wf_level :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Level@n : LevelSort )
A level is a literal, a successor, or a join. Level@n is the type of the levels below ω·(n+1), so a literal is of the sorts at least its tier.
| wf_llit :
  `( fst o <= n ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ 𝕃ᵒ o : Level@n )
The successor of a level.
| wf_succl :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ succl M : Level@n )
The join of two levels.
| wf_maxl :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl M N : Level@n )
The universe of propositions is a small type, at the least level. A proposition is a type, but no universe Type@{L} contains it.
| wf_prop :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Propₘ : Type@0 )
The true proposition.
| wf_True :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ⊤ : Propₘ )
The introduction of ⊤.
| wf_tt :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tt : ⊤ )
The false proposition.
| wf_False :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ⊥ : Propₘ )
Ex falso: a proof of ⊥ is a term of every type, of either sort, whose result may come from a proof (level_closed_sort): never a level, as it would put a proof inside a level.
| wf_absurd :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ C : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     level_closed_sort Propₘ Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : ⊥ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ efq M return C : C )
The dependent conjunction of propositions.
| wf_and :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{ak_propositional} P ⊢ Q : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Σₚ P Q : Propₘ )
The proof of the conjunction Σₚ P Q from proofs of its components; the components' types are the annotation.
| wf_conj :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{ak_propositional} P ⊢ Q : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : P ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : Q[Id,,M] ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_conj P Q M N : Σₚ P Q )
The proof of the first component of a conjunction.
| wf_left :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{ak_propositional} P ⊢ Q : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Σₚ P Q ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_left M : P )
The proof of the second component, at the first. Its type is premised to be a proposition, as the type of wf_tuple is: reflexivity at a proof is proof irrelevance, which needs its type typed before substitution is.
| wf_right :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{ak_propositional} P ⊢ Q : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Σₚ P Q ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Q[Id,,a_left M] : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_right M : Q[Id,,a_left M] )
A proof tagged with its proposition, of that proposition. It is equal to the proof by proof irrelevance (wf_exp_eq_irrelevant).
| wf_proof_tag :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : P ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_proof P M : P )
The type former of a declared member of a group of inductive types, of the type the declaration gives: a Π over its parameters of the sort.
| wf_ind :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D k = Some M ->
     k < ind_ndecl D ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_ind p k : ind_ty D M )
A constructor of a member: a Π over the parameters and the arguments of the member at the parameters. At a view, the view's own parameters and arguments, into the container's member at the view's arguments: the normal form of a value read at a view (wf_exp_eq_con_view). The type is a closed type, of a well-formed context of arguments, and the rest of the type of a recursive argument after any number of its shape's domains is a type, under those domains: all follow from the declaration, and are premises so that the semantic models read them off the derivation.
| wf_con :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D k = Some M ->
     ind_con M c = Some gs ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ cargs_ctx p D M gs ++ im_params D M ->
     (forall gs1 t gs2 j, gs = gs1 ++ ca_rec t :: gs2 -> j <= List.length (ptyp_doms t) ->
        ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ (shape_domains_ctx (cargs_pat gs1) (List.firstn j (ptyp_doms t)) ++ cargs_ctx p D M gs1 ++ im_params D M)
                  ▹{ak_relevant} ptyp_ty p D (im_nn M) (List.repeat false j ++ cargs_pat gs1) (ptyp_skip j t)) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ⋅ ⊢ con_ty p D k M gs : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_con p k c : con_ty p D k M gs )
The eliminator of the group at p, at the member m, at the parameters Ps (the group's uniform ones, then the member's non-uniform ones): one block per member of the group, in order, each with its motive under the member's non-uniform parameters and the scrutinee, its scrutinee type, the member's type there, and its branches, one per constructor in order, under the non-uniform parameters, the constructor's arguments and the recursive results, the result of an argument recursive in the member j being at the motive of j. The parameters are typed one by one, at the instances of their telescope. The eliminator carries the uniform parameters Us, those of the scrutinee's type: the scrutinee and each block's scrutinee type are at the members' types at them. The motives are all of one sort S: all types of a universe, or all propositions (then the eliminator is a proof, never evaluated); no elimination mixes the two. The record views have no block (there are ind_nblk D blocks, for the members before them), and a recursive argument at a record view has the results of its fields' leaf paths. The premises on the motives' and the branches' contexts range over every member, the record views too; this is harmless: a record view's motive context is its record type at Us and its branch context its fields with their leaf paths' results, both well formed by the declaration, and no block reads them.
| wf_elim :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D m = Some Mm ->
     List.nth_error Bks m = Some bm ->
     List.length Bks = ind_nblk D ->
     List.length Ps = im_np D Mm ->
     (forall k P T, nth_error Ps k = Some P -> nth_error (tele_insts (im_params D Mm) Id Ps) k = Some T ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : T) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : ind_mty p D m (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps) (List.skipn (ind_nu D) Ps) ->
     Us = List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps ->
     (forall k Mk b, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> List.nth_error Bks k = Some b -> eb_binder_count b = S (im_nn Mk)) ->
     (forall k Mk b, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> List.nth_error Bks k = Some b ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ tele_sub (im_nparams Mk) (sb_of_list Id (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ▹{ak_relevant} eb_scrutinee_type b
                     ≈ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->
     (forall k Mk b, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> List.nth_error Bks k = Some b ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps) ++ Γ ⊢ eb_motive b : abs_kind_sort r Typeω@i) ->
     (forall k Mk, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps) ≈ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->
     (forall k Mk b, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> List.nth_error Bks k = Some b -> brs_names (im_cons Mk) (eb_brs b)) ->
     (forall k Mk c gs, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> ind_con Mk c = Some gs ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ elim_bctx r p D Mk gs (blocks_motives Bks) (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)
                     ≈ elim_bctx r p D Mk gs (blocks_motives Bks) (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->
     (forall k Mk b c gs n B, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> List.nth_error Bks k = Some b ->
        ind_con Mk c = Some gs -> In (c, n, B) (eb_brs b) ->
        n = (im_nn Mk + List.length gs + cargs_nrec D gs)%nat) ->
     (forall k Mk b c gs n B, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> List.nth_error Bks k = Some b ->
        ind_con Mk c = Some gs -> In (c, n, B) (eb_brs b) ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ elim_bctx r p D Mk gs (blocks_motives Bks) (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps) ++ Γ ⊢ B
          : elim_branch_type p D k Mk c gs (eb_motive b) (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->
     motive_kind r ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_elim r p Us m Bks M : (eb_motive bm)[sb_of_list Id (List.skipn (ind_nu D) Ps ++ M :: nil)] )
A Π out of a domain of the kind κd into a codomain of the kind κc (pi_kinds): a type of functions, in a universe its domain and codomain are in, small or large (a domain of another kind is in Prop or LevelSort); the impredicative ∀, into a family of propositions; or a type of levels, between types of levels. The codomain's universe is the weakening of the domain's: a universe that mentions the bound variable has no name here. At κd = κc = ak_level the universe U plays no part.
| wf_pi :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵤ U ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : abs_kind_sort κd U ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A ⊢ B : (abs_kind_sort κc U)[↑]ʷ ->
     pi_kinds κd κc ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_pi κd κc A B : abs_kind_sort κc U )
A λ-abstraction, over a type of the kind κd, into a type of the kind κc: a function, a proof of a ∀, or a function between levels (pi_kinds).
| wf_fn :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     sort_kind Srt κd ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A ⊢ B : abs_kind_sort κc Typeω@i ->
     pi_kinds κd κc ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A ⊢ M : B ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ λ A M : a_pi κd κc A B )
An application, at the codomain instantiated by the argument: of a function, or of a proof of a ∀.
| wf_app :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     sort_kind Srt κd ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A ⊢ B : abs_kind_sort κc Typeω@i ->
     pi_kinds κd κc ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : a_pi κd κc A B ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M $ N : B[Id,,N] )
A local definition, of its annotated type. The body's type is of a sort the binding's sort may build (level_closed_sort): a level only under a definition of a level.
| wf_let :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ A ≔ M ⊢ C : SrtC ->
     level_closed_sort Srt SrtC ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ A ≔ M ⊢ B : C ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ℓ A ≔ M in B : C[Id,,M] )
A local module occupies one index, a slot holding its unit. The body's type is premised to be a type, as the canonical type of wf_mem is: equivalent substitutions are moved through the body by ζ, and the two sides then meet at that type.
| wf_let_mod :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵘ U ≈ U ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹ₘ U ⊢ C : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     module_body_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹ₘ U ⊢ B : C ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ℓₘ U in B : C[Id ,,ₘ me_lit U] )
A local definition with a module part: its term part as a definition of a type of a large universe, as a definition with a module part is relevant (wf_ext_eq_dm), and its module part an alias under no parameters, as the command's is; the body's type premised to be a type as for wf_let_mod
| wf_let_dm :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵘ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ≈ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ⊢ C : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     module_body_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ⊢ B : C ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ℓᵈ A ≔ M ‖ (gu_mk nil (md_alias E)) in B : C[Id ,,ᵈ M ‖ me_lit (gu_mk nil (md_alias E))] )
A member: the module expression is well formed and looks the member up (mdenote of the selection) as a term, at the type the lookup reads. This is the only typing rule for members. The type is premised to be a type, as the induction moving a typing along equivalent substitutions needs it, and the δ-reduct, if any, to inhabit it, as soundness needs it. A filed axiom or abstract definition read bare has no δ-reduct (mdesc_named), so the premise never asks for the member itself.
| wf_mem :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵐ H ≈ H ->
     mdenote Θ Ξ Γ (me_mem H x) R ->
     mdesc_type R = Some A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     (forall M, mdesc_reduct R = Some M -> Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_mem H x : A )
A variable, at the type the context gives it.
| wf_vlookup :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Γ ∋ #x : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ #x : A )
The type former of a record, of the type its declaration gives: a Π over its parameters of its sort. The facts about the declaration are premises, as for wf_con, so that the semantic models read them off the derivation: the field names are distinct, the parameters are assumptions, the type is a closed type, the fields' context is well formed, the sort is a universe over the parameters, and each field is a type in the sort, or a proposition, as its stored relevance says, over the fields before it and the parameters.
| wf_record :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.NoDup (List.map fst (record_fields R)) ->
     all_assumptions (record_params R) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ⋅ ⊢ record_ty R : Typeω@i ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_fctx R (List.length (record_fields R)) ++ record_params R ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_params R ⊢ᵤ record_sort R ->
     (forall k f T, List.nth_error (record_fields R) k = Some (f, T) ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_fctx R k ++ record_params R ⊢ T : abs_kind_sort (record_field_kind R k) (record_sort R)[wk_shiftn k]ʷ) ->
     List.length (record_field_kinds R) = List.length (record_fields R) ->
     (forall k, field_kind (record_field_kind R k)) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_record p : record_ty R )
An element of a record type T, the type former at the parameters Ns: the fields by name in the declaration's order, each at its type at the parameters and the values of the fields before it. T is premised to be a type, as the type of wf_mem is.
| wf_tuple :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ T : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ T ≈ apps_exp (a_record p) Ns : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_record p : record_ty R ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.length Ns = List.length (record_params R) ->
     (forall k N A, List.nth_error Ns k = Some N -> List.nth_error (tele_insts (record_params R) Id Ns) k = Some A ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : A) ->
     List.map fst fs = List.map fst (record_fields R) ->
     (forall k f M U, List.nth_error fs k = Some (f, M) -> List.nth_error (record_fields R) k = Some (f, U) ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : U[sb_of_list Id (Ns ++ List.firstn k (List.map snd fs))]) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tuple T fs : T )
A field, at its type at the parameters and the projections of the fields before it. That type is premised to be a type, as the type of wf_mem is.
| wf_proj :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : apps_exp (a_record p) Ns ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_record p : record_ty R ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.length Ns = List.length (record_params R) ->
     (forall k N A, List.nth_error Ns k = Some N -> List.nth_error (tele_insts (record_params R) Id Ns) k = Some A ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : A) ->
     List.nth_error (record_fields R) k = Some (f, U) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ U[sb_of_list Id (Ns ++ record_pre R k M)] : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_proj f M : U[sb_of_list Id (Ns ++ record_pre R k M)] )
Subsumption: a term is at every type above its type.
| wf_exp_subtyp :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     
This premise is needed for soundness. It is asymmetric: only A' is checked. Checking A as well would make even Γ ⊢ Typeω@0[↑]ʷ : Typeω@1 underivable, since weakening it would require Γ ⊢ Typeω@1[↑]ʷ : Typeω@2, which requires Γ ⊢ Typeω@2[↑]ʷ : Typeω@3, and so on.
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A' : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A ⊆ A' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A' )
where "Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A" := (wf_exp Θ Ξ Γ A M) : type_scope

with wf_exp_eq : gdeps -> gstack -> ctx -> typ -> exp -> exp -> Prop :=

Congruence rules

| wf_exp_eq_typ_cong :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Typeω@i ≈ Typeω@i : Typeω@(S i) )
| wf_exp_eq_univ_cong :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Type⟨M⟩ ≈ Type⟨M'⟩ : Type⟨succl M⟩ )
| wf_exp_eq_level_cong :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Level@n ≈ Level@n : LevelSort )
| wf_exp_eq_llit_cong :
  `( fst o <= n ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ 𝕃ᵒ o ≈ 𝕃ᵒ o : Level@n )
| wf_exp_eq_succl_cong :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ succl M ≈ succl M' : Level@n )
| wf_exp_eq_maxl_cong :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N ≈ N' : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl M N ≈ maxl M' N' : Level@n )

The Level Equations

Levels are a join semilattice with a least element and an inflationary successor that distributes over the join; the literal ω·a + b is the b-th successor of the limit ω·a, and the limit ω·(n+1) is above every level of sort n (absorption). These are the equations of Danielsson–Favier–Kubánek Fig. 2 and absorption, and they are complete for the canonical forms of Core.Syntactic.Levels.Levels: two levels are equal exactly when they have the same canonical form.
| wf_exp_eq_llit_succl :
  `( a <= n ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ 𝕃ᵒ(a, S b) ≈ succl (𝕃ᵒ(a, b)) : Level@n )
| wf_exp_eq_maxl_absorb :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl M (𝕃ᵒ(S n, 0)) ≈ 𝕃ᵒ(S n, 0) : Level@(S n) )
| wf_exp_eq_maxl_zero :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl (𝕃@0) M ≈ M : Level@n )
| wf_exp_eq_maxl_assoc :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl (maxl M N) P ≈ maxl M (maxl N P) : Level@n )
| wf_exp_eq_maxl_comm :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl M N ≈ maxl N M : Level@n )
| wf_exp_eq_maxl_idem :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl M M ≈ M : Level@n )
| wf_exp_eq_succl_maxl :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : Level@n ->

  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->

                     ≈ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->
     (forall k Mk b, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> List.nth_error Bks' k = Some b ->

                     ≈ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->

     (forall k Mk, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps) ≈ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->

        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ elim_bctx r p D Mk gs (blocks_motives Bks) (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)

ι: the eliminator on a constructor is the constructor's branch, at the non-uniform parameters, the arguments and the recursive results (elim_ihs): the eliminator at a recursive argument, and at one of a function shape λ x. elim (f x). The arguments are typed one by one, at the instances of their telescope at the parameters.

                     ≈ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->

        ind_con Mk c = Some gs -> In (c, n, B) (eb_brs b) ->

The eliminator at a view is the eliminator of the view's own group at the container's member, its blocks those of the members of this group that are the container's group's members at the view's arguments (view_wrap, E1′): a stuck eliminator at a view is a stuck one of the container, at the container's uniform parameters (the view's arguments) when the container's group has views too. The view's arguments are as many as the container's uniform parameters, as the declaration says; the premise lets the wrapped blocks' scrutinee types, the container's member types at them, be read off the rule.

     (forall k Mk, ind_member D k = Some Mk -> Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps) ≈ elim_mctx p D k Mk (List.firstn (ind_nu D) Ps)) ->

A constructor of a view at the group's uniform parameters Us is the container's constructor at the view's arguments there, both sides at the same type.
| wf_exp_eq_con_view :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->

     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ apps_exp (a_con qc k c) (im_pre Mj Us ++ Ms) : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ apps_exp (a_con p j c) (Us ++ Ms) ≈ apps_exp (a_con qc k c) (im_pre Mj Us ++ Ms) : A )
The constructor of a record view at the group's uniform parameters Us and the fields Ms is the tuple of the fields, by name, at the record type at the view's instance there, both sides at the same type. The constructor is the view's own (ind_con), as in wf_con: it takes its fields at their sorts, which are the record's (rview_struct_kinds), as the tuple does.
| wf_exp_eq_con_rview :
  `( ind_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some D ->
     ind_member D j = Some Mj ->
     im_head Mj = mh_record qr Is fl ->
     ind_con Mj c = Some gs ->
     List.length Us = ind_nu D ->
     List.length Ms = List.length fl ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ apps_exp (a_con p j c) (Us ++ Ms) : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tuple (apps_exp (a_record qr) (im_pre Mj Us)) (List.combine fl Ms) : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ apps_exp (a_con p j c) (Us ++ Ms) ≈ a_tuple (apps_exp (a_record qr) (im_pre Mj Us)) (List.combine fl Ms) : A )
ζ: a local definition is substituted into its body.
| wf_exp_eq_let_zeta :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ A ≔ M ⊢ C : SrtC ->
     level_closed_sort Srt SrtC ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ A ≔ M ⊢ B : C ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ℓ A ≔ M in B ≈ B[Id,,M] : C[Id,,M] )
ζ for local modules: the slot is replaced by the unit.
| wf_exp_eq_let_mod_zeta :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵘ U ≈ U ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹ₘ U ⊢ C : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     module_body_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹ₘ U ⊢ B : C ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ℓₘ U in B ≈ B[Id ,,ₘ me_lit U] : C[Id ,,ₘ me_lit U] )
ζ for a local definition with a module part: both parts are substituted
| wf_exp_eq_let_dm_zeta :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵘ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ≈ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ⊢ C : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     module_body_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ⊢ B : C ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ ℓᵈ A ≔ M ‖ (gu_mk nil (md_alias E)) in B ≈ B[Id ,,ᵈ M ‖ me_lit (gu_mk nil (md_alias E))]
       : C[Id ,,ᵈ M ‖ me_lit (gu_mk nil (md_alias E))] )
δ for members: a member is the δ-reduct the lookup reads: the body of a transparent definition at the arguments, the name of a filed axiom or abstract definition at them, or a type former.
| wf_exp_eq_mem_delta :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵐ H ≈ H ->
     mdenote Θ Ξ Γ (me_mem H x) R ->
     mdesc_type R = Some A ->
     mdesc_reduct R = Some M ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_mem H x ≈ M : A )
δ for local definitions: a defined variable is its body. It is stated at every depth, since weakening moves a definition arbitrarily deep.
| wf_exp_eq_var_delta :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Γ ∋ #x ≔ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ #x ≈ M : A )

Uniqueness rule

| wf_exp_eq_fn_eta :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     sort_kind Srt κd ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A ⊢ B : abs_kind_sort κc Typeω@i ->
     pi_kinds κd κc ->

Proof irrelevance: two proofs of a proposition are equal.
| wf_exp_eq_irrelevant :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ P : Propₘ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : P ->

     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : P )

Records

The record type former is equal to itself, with the premises of wf_record.
| wf_exp_eq_record_cong :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.NoDup (List.map fst (record_fields R)) ->
     all_assumptions (record_params R) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ ⋅ ⊢ record_ty R : Typeω@i ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_fctx R (List.length (record_fields R)) ++ record_params R ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_params R ⊢ᵤ record_sort R ->
     (forall k f T, List.nth_error (record_fields R) k = Some (f, T) ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_fctx R k ++ record_params R ⊢ T : abs_kind_sort (record_field_kind R k) (record_sort R)[wk_shiftn k]ʷ) ->
     List.length (record_field_kinds R) = List.length (record_fields R) ->
     (forall k, field_kind (record_field_kind R k)) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_record p ≈ a_record p : record_ty R )
Record elements of equal types with equal fields, both sides typed. The parameters are typed and the field names are the declaration's, as in wf_tuple: the semantic models relate the two tuples at the record type only at parameters they read as valid.
| wf_exp_eq_tuple_cong :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tuple T fs : T ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ T ≈ T' : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ T ≈ apps_exp (a_record p) Ns : Typeω@i ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.length Ns = List.length (record_params R) ->
     (forall k N A, List.nth_error Ns k = Some N -> List.nth_error (tele_insts (record_params R) Id Ns) k = Some A ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : A) ->
     List.map fst fs = List.map fst (record_fields R) ->
     List.map fst fs' = List.map fst fs ->
     (forall k f M M' U, List.nth_error fs k = Some (f, M) -> List.nth_error fs' k = Some (f, M') ->
        List.nth_error (record_fields R) k = Some (f, U) ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : U[sb_of_list Id (Ns ++ List.firstn k (List.map snd fs))]) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tuple T' fs' : T ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tuple T fs ≈ a_tuple T' fs' : T )
The fields of equal records, at the field's type at the parameters and the projections of the fields before it, with the premises of wf_proj: the semantic models relate the two projections only at the field's type; at any other type they are equal by subsumption. The right-hand side is premised at that type, as for wf_exp_eq_tuple_cong: its own type is at the projections of M', equal to it only by this rule at the fields before.
| wf_exp_eq_proj_cong :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : apps_exp (a_record p) Ns ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_record p : record_ty R ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.length Ns = List.length (record_params R) ->
     (forall k N A, List.nth_error Ns k = Some N -> List.nth_error (tele_insts (record_params R) Id Ns) k = Some A ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ N : A) ->
     List.nth_error (record_fields R) k = Some (f, U) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ U[sb_of_list Id (Ns ++ record_pre R k M)] : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_proj f M' : U[sb_of_list Id (Ns ++ record_pre R k M)] ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_proj f M ≈ a_proj f M' : U[sb_of_list Id (Ns ++ record_pre R k M)] )
Field-β: the field of a record element is its first field so named. Both sides are premised to be of the type: the field's type at the element's projections and at its fields are equal only by the field-β of the fields before it. The field is relevant: at a proposition the two sides are equal by wf_exp_eq_irrelevant (see tuple_proj_eq). The record type and the field's position name its sort.
| wf_exp_eq_field_beta :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tuple T fs : T ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ T ≈ apps_exp (a_record p) Ns : Typeω@i ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     field_index fs f = Some k ->
     record_field_kind R k = ak_relevant ->
     field_lookup fs f = Some M ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_proj f (a_tuple T fs) : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_proj f (a_tuple T fs) ≈ M : A )
η for records: an element is the tuple of its projections. The parameters are all given, as in wf_tuple: the semantic models read the record type only at all its parameters.
| wf_exp_eq_record_eta :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : apps_exp (a_record p) Ns ->
     record_lookup Θ Ξ p = Some R ->
     List.length Ns = List.length (record_params R) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_tuple (apps_exp (a_record p) Ns) (record_eta_fields R M) : apps_exp (a_record p) Ns ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ a_tuple (apps_exp (a_record p) Ns) (record_eta_fields R M) : apps_exp (a_record p) Ns )

Subsumption and the PER rules

| wf_exp_eq_subtyp :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A' : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     
This premise mirrors the one of wf_exp_subtyp.
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A ⊆ A' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : A' )
| wf_exp_eq_sym :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M' ≈ M : A )
| wf_exp_eq_trans :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M' ≈ M'' : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M'' : A )
where "Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : A" := (wf_exp_eq Θ Ξ Γ A M M') : type_scope

Subtyping

with wf_subtyp : gdeps -> gstack -> ctx -> typ -> typ -> Prop :=
| wf_subtyp_refl :
  
This premise lets the presupposition lemmas be proved independently: it gives presupposition for the right-hand side directly.
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M' : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ⊆ M' )
| wf_subtyp_trans :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ⊆ M' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M' ⊆ M'' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M ⊆ M'' )
| wf_subtyp_univ :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     i < j ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Typeω@i ⊆ Typeω@j )
A small universe below one at a larger level. The order on levels is maxl M M' ≈ M', which is decidable on canonical forms (Core.Syntactic.Levels.Levels.lvl_le) and never the order on realisers.
| wf_subtyp_suniv :
  
The two typings let the presupposition lemmas be proved independently, as in wf_subtyp_refl.
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M' : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ maxl M M' ≈ M' : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Type⟨M⟩ ⊆ Type⟨M'⟩ )
A type of levels is below every type of levels of a larger sort: every level of a sort is a level of each larger one.
| wf_subtyp_level :
  `( m <= n ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Level@m ⊆ Level@n )
A small universe below every large one.
| wf_subtyp_small_large :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ M : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ Type⟨M⟩ ⊆ Typeω@i )
A Π into an evaluated kind is covariant in the codomain, out of equal domains: into a type of a universe, or between types of levels, as types of levels are ordered by their sorts (wf_subtyp_level). A ∀ is a proposition, so it is only related by wf_subtyp_refl.
| wf_subtyp_pi :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A : abs_kind_sort κd Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A' : abs_kind_sort κd Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A ≈ A' : abs_kind_sort κd Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A ⊢ B : abs_kind_sort κc Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A' ⊢ B' : abs_kind_sort κc Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ▹{κd} A' ⊢ B ⊆ B' ->
     pi_kinds κd κc ->
     evaluated_kind κc ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ a_pi κd κc A B ⊆ a_pi κd κc A' B' )
where "Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ A ⊆ A'" := (wf_subtyp Θ Ξ Γ A A') : type_scope

Universes

Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵤ U: U is a universe, large or small at a level of Γ.
with wf_is_univ : gdeps -> gstack -> ctx -> typ -> Prop :=
| wf_is_univ_large :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵤ Typeω@i )
| wf_is_univ_small :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ L : Level@n ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵤ Type⟨L⟩ )
where "Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ᵤ U" := (wf_is_univ Θ Ξ Γ U) : type_scope



Modules

Equivalence of modules is pointwise: two units are equivalent when their entries are, one by one and in the same order, and two module expressions when their parts are. Well-formedness is the reflexive instance.
Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ≈ Ψ' compares two extensions of Γ entry by entry. An entry is compared in the left extension; the right one's entry is also typed in the right extension, so that presupposition needs no context conversion.
with wf_ext_eq : gdeps -> gstack -> ctx -> ctx -> ctx -> Prop :=
| wf_ext_eq_nil :
  `( ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ ⋅ ≈ ⋅ )
An assumption: the two types are each below the other, each a type of its own sort, so that equations chain whatever sorts the middle type is given (wf_subtyp_trans); that the sorts agree is the same-sort theorem, after completeness.
| wf_ext_eq_ass :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ≈ Ψ' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     sort_kind Srt κ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ' ++ Γ ⊢ A' : Srt' ->
     sort_kind Srt' κ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A ⊆ A' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A' ⊆ A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ▹{κ} A ≈ Ψ' ▹{κ} A' )
A definition: its types as an assumption's, and equal bodies.
| wf_ext_eq_def :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ≈ Ψ' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A : Srt ->
     type_sort Srt ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ' ++ Γ ⊢ A' : Srt' ->
     type_sort Srt' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A ⊆ A' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A' ⊆ A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ' ++ Γ ⊢ M' : A' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ▸ A ≔ M ≈ Ψ' ▸ A' ≔ M' )
| wf_ext_eq_mod :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ≈ Ψ' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ᵘ U ≈ U' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ' ++ Γ ⊢ᵘ U' ≈ U' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ▹ₘ U ≈ Ψ' ▹ₘ U' )
A definition with a module part: as a definition and as a module slot, an alias under no parameters (wf_ctx_extend_dm).
| wf_ext_eq_dm :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ≈ Ψ' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ A ≈ A' : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ M : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ M ≈ M' : A ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ' ++ Γ ⊢ A' : Typeω@i ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ' ++ Γ ⊢ M' : A' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ ++ Γ ⊢ᵘ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ≈ gu_mk nil (md_alias E') ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Ψ' ++ Γ ⊢ᵘ gu_mk nil (md_alias E') ≈ gu_mk nil (md_alias E') ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ▸ₘ A ≔ M ‖ gu_mk nil (md_alias E) ≈ Ψ' ▸ₘ A' ≔ M' ‖ gu_mk nil (md_alias E') )
where "Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Ψ ≈ Ψ'" := (wf_ext_eq Θ Ξ Γ Ψ Ψ') : type_scope

Units. Each side of a body unit is well formed where it stands: its body, read as the entries its local opens generate (body_xp), and its parameters form an extension of Γ, and the target of each open is a module there. The two sides have the same shape as written, opens at the same places with the same items, and as expanded (body_shape), and are compared entry by entry through their expansions; the targets of the opens are compared pairwise, filled in like the entries. Each entry is compared with the entries before it filled in (gm_fill: a definition by its body, a module by its unit), in the left parameters' context, and each filled-in entry of the right side is typed in the right parameters' context, as the parts of an extension are: so the comparison never reads one side's entries in the other side's body. An entry is compared through its parts: its term part (entry_tm) as a definition is, and its module part (entry_unit) as a module is, so a definition with a module part is compared as both. Every entry can be filled in: a local body has no bodiless definition and no inductive type. entry_sort y is the sort of definition y's type: a large universe or Prop by the entry's kind (entry_kind) on either side, as for a global definition, or LevelSort. Entries of a type of levels are governed by the flag premise alone: with lv = true every parameter is a type of levels (level_sorted_parameters); with lv = false the body has no member of a type of levels (⊢ⁿˡ: every definition of the expanded body, private ones included, has a type of a universe). So module M (n : ℕ) where def v : Level ≔ 0l end is rejected, and module K (u : Level) where def w : Level ≔ u end is accepted.
with wf_unit_eq : gdeps -> gstack -> ctx -> gunit -> gunit -> Prop :=
| wf_unit_eq_body :
  `( body_xp Θ Ξ (Δ ++ Γ) Φ Φx ->
     body_xp Θ Ξ (Δ' ++ Γ) Φ' Φx' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ Δ ≈ Δ' ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ body_ctx Φx ++ Δ ≈ body_ctx Φx ++ Δ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ˣ body_ctx Φx' ++ Δ' ≈ body_ctx Φx' ++ Δ' ->
     (forall y, type_sort (entry_sort y)) ->
     (forall y Φ0 E A M, gm_prefix_upto Φx y = Some (gm_ext Φ0 y E) -> entry_tm E = Some (A, M) ->
        sort_kind (entry_sort y) (entry_kind E)) ->
     (forall y Φ0' E' A' M', gm_prefix_upto Φx' y = Some (gm_ext Φ0' y E') -> entry_tm E' = Some (A', M') ->
        sort_kind (entry_sort y) (entry_kind E')) ->
     (forall y Φ0 E A M Φ0' E' A' M' σ σ',
        gm_prefix_upto Φx y = Some (gm_ext Φ0 y E) -> entry_tm E = Some (A, M) ->
        gm_prefix_upto Φx' y = Some (gm_ext Φ0' y E') -> entry_tm E' = Some (A', M') ->
        gm_fill Φ0 = Some σ -> gm_fill Φ0' = Some σ' ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Δ ++ Γ ⊢ A[σ] : entry_sort y) ->
     (forall y Φ0 E A M Φ0' E' A' M' σ σ',
        gm_prefix_upto Φx y = Some (gm_ext Φ0 y E) -> entry_tm E = Some (A, M) ->
        gm_prefix_upto Φx' y = Some (gm_ext Φ0' y E') -> entry_tm E' = Some (A', M') ->
        gm_fill Φ0 = Some σ -> gm_fill Φ0' = Some σ' ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Δ ++ Γ ⊢ A[σ] ≈ A'[σ'] : entry_sort y) ->
     (forall y Φ0 E A M Φ0' E' A' M' σ σ',

A module expression is a module when the module part of what it denotes has a telescope (mdesc_mod_tele), and an argument is checked against the outermost parameter of that telescope (tele_view): a module is applied to at most as many arguments as it has parameters. Both arguments are typed, as the parts of an extension are, and so is the parameter's type.

Descriptions With No Member of a Type of Levels

Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Γ ⊢ⁿˡ R: no member of the module description R, read in Γ, has a type of levels: every term it holds, directly or in a module it holds, is of the kind of a large universe or of a proposition. A description is abstracted over the parameters of an alias (mdesc_up), which turns a member of type A into one of type Π Δ. A; over a parameter of a universe that is no type when A is a type of levels, so an alias or a body with such a parameter asks this of its target (no_level_members, levels_abstractable). The judgment walks the description as member lookup reads it, and reads the kinds the entries are tagged with, not their typings: the typing of a description is desc_ok's, and with the tags it gives the abstracted types. So, of a well-formed module expression, it is decided by walking what the expression denotes. The descriptions of module entries are arguments of the rules, so that every premise is positive.

A closed module, by its stored entries: each definition is of the kind of a large universe or of a proposition; every other entry, read as it is stored (ge_read), denotes (member_descs) a description with no member of a type of levels; stored entries are closed, so they are read at ⋅, in a well-formed global context. The location is a filed body (gc_body: a loaded unit or a finished submodule) with exactly these entries, no open frame: an open frame grows, and an entry filed later is read through every description of the frame. In module F where module A (n : ℕ) ≔ F; def w : Level ≔ 0l end the member w of A would be of Π (n : ℕ) Level, so an alias with a parameter of a universe of a still open frame is rejected.

Well-formedness of the Global Context

Part of the same mutual definition: an entry's type and body are checked by the term judgments, and a use of a global appeals to ⊢ᵍ Θ ⍮ Ξ.
A unit is checked against the units filed before it, and a frame against the frames outside it, which is why both components are indices of the whole block.
A member of a parameterized module is checked in the telescope of parameters it lives under, and stored generalized over it (ctx_pi, ctx_fn). ge_mod records only the parameters it adds to that telescope; a gunit records all of it, which is why a unit is checked at ⋅.
Canonicity is part of well-formedness: wf_gmod_ext asks for freshness, so a well-formed context resolves deterministically without a separate condition.
An entry is checked against the current module, which is the head of Ξ: that frame is what wf_gmod_ext pushed, and it carries the parameters and the members declared so far. The local context is the telescope of all the frames' parameters, gs_tele Ξ: parameters are ordinary λ-variables. A definition is stored generalized over that telescope, so what is filed is closed, and nothing has to be done to it when it is read anywhere else. mp is the entry's own module path, which a nested module's frame is named by.

A definition or an axiom: its type is of the sort of its kind r — a type of a universe, a proposition, or a type of levels — and its body, if it has one, carries the type. It is filed generalized over the parameters by Π types into the kind (ctx_pi_at r), so that a propositional member stays a proposition and a level a level. A definition of a type of levels has only types of levels as the frames' parameters (level_sorted_parameters), so that what is filed is a type: def ofNat (n : ℕ) : Level is rejected.

A record type, with parameters Δ over the frames' parameters, before the members of its module: its sort is a universe over the parameters, its field names are distinct, and each field is a type in the sort over the fields before it and the parameters. The record is not filed while its fields are checked, so no field mentions it: records are not recursive, by construction. No type of the declaration has a free module variable (record_mvc), as no type in a context of assumptions.
| wf_gentry_record :
  `( record_params R = Δ ++ gs_tele Ξ ->
     all_assumptions (record_params R) ->
     record_mvc R ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_params R ⊢ᵤ record_sort R ->
     List.NoDup (List.map fst (record_fields R)) ->
     (forall k f T, List.nth_error (record_fields R) k = Some (f, T) ->
        Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ record_fctx R k ++ record_params R ⊢ T : abs_kind_sort (record_field_kind R k) (record_sort R)[wk_shiftn k]ʷ) ->
     List.length (record_field_kinds R) = List.length (record_fields R) ->
     (forall k, field_kind (record_field_kind R k)) ->
     
the record's own parameters are types of a universe or types of levels, not propositions, as a unit's are: param_sorts gives their sorts
     (forall k, parameter_sort param_level (param_sorts k)) ->
     (forall Δ1 κ T Δ2, Δ = Δ1 ++ ce_ass κ T :: Δ2 -> Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Δ2 ++ gs_tele Ξ ⊢ T : param_sorts (List.length Δ2)) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⊢ᵉ ge_record pv mp R ⋄ )
A record type with the body of its module: the body is checked as an ordinary module over the record's own parameters and then a value of the record (record_self), in the record's open frame, which carries the declaration (fk_record); the declaration itself is checked where the module starts (wf_gmod_record_nil). The record is filed only when its frame closes.
| wf_gentry_record_body :
  `( record_params R = Δ ++ gs_tele Ξ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ fk_record R ⍮ ce_ass (sort_exp_kind (record_sort R)) (record_self mp R) :: Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ Φ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⊢ᵉ ge_record pv mp R Φ )
where "Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⊢ᵉ E" := (wf_gentry Θ Ξ mp E) : type_scope

The module at path mp, of kind K, with own parameters Δ, a telescope over the frames' parameters gs_tele Ξ.
with wf_gmod : gdeps -> gstack -> qname -> frame_kind -> ctx -> gmod -> Prop :=
An ordinary module, before its members
| wf_gmod_nil :
  `( all_assumptions Δ ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Δ ++ gs_tele Ξ ->
     
The parameters are types of a universe or types of levels, as a unit's are: param_sorts gives their sorts
     (forall k, parameter_sort param_level (param_sorts k)) ->
     (forall Δ1 κ T Δ2, Δ = Δ1 ++ ce_ass κ T :: Δ2 -> Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ Δ2 ++ gs_tele Ξ ⊢ T : param_sorts (List.length Δ2)) ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ fk_module ⍮ Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ ⋄ )
The module of the declared member k of the group D at pq, before its members: the member's declaration, checked as an entry with an empty module (wf_gentry_ind_nil, wf_gentry_ind_mem_nil), and the module's parameters, the uniform ones, over the frames' parameters, as wf_gmod_nil has them. A member is declared in an enclosing frame, so its module is no unit.
| wf_gmod_ind_nil :
  `( all_assumptions Δ ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ Δ ++ gs_tele ((mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ) ->
     
The parameters are types of a universe or types of levels, as for wf_gmod_nil
     (forall k, parameter_sort param_level (param_sorts k)) ->
     (forall Δ1 κ T Δ2, Δ = Δ1 ++ ce_ass κ T :: Δ2 ->
        Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ Δ2 ++ gs_tele ((mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ) ⊢ T : param_sorts (List.length Δ2)) ->
     Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ mp ⊢ᵉ ge_ind pv pq k D ⋄ ->
     ind_uparams D = Δ ++ gs_tele ((mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ) ->
     Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ fk_ind pq k D ⍮ Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ ⋄ )
The module of the record type R, before its members: the record's declaration, checked as an entry with an empty module (wf_gentry_record), and the module's parameters: the record's own, over the frames' parameters, as wf_gmod_nil has them, and then a value of the record (record_self). The value's type names the record, found only inside the record's frame, so it is typed there (as wf_gs_tele shows), not here (frame_params). A record is declared in an enclosing frame, so its module is no unit.
| wf_gmod_record_nil :
  `( all_assumptions Δ ->
     ⊢ Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ Δ ++ gs_tele ((mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ) ->
     
The parameters are types of a universe or types of levels, as for wf_gmod_nil; the value's type is a record type, of a universe, where it is typed
     (forall k, parameter_sort param_level (param_sorts k)) ->
     (forall Δ1 κ T Δ2, Δ = Δ1 ++ ce_ass κ T :: Δ2 ->
        Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ Δ2 ++ gs_tele ((mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ) ⊢ T : param_sorts (List.length Δ2)) ->
     Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ mp ⊢ᵉ ge_record pv mp R ⋄ ->
     record_params R = Δ ++ gs_tele ((mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ) ->
     Θ ⍮ (mq, Kq, Uq) :: Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ fk_record R ⍮ ce_ass (sort_exp_kind (record_sort R)) (record_self mp R) :: Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ ⋄ )
The entry is checked against the members declared before it: the module so far is gu_mk Δ Φ, pushed as the innermost frame under its own path, of the module's kind.
| wf_gmod_ext :
  `( Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ K ⍮ Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ Φ ->
     Θ ⍮ (mp, K, gu_body Δ Φ) :: Ξ ⍮ qname_in mp x ⊢ᵉ E ->
     gm_fresh x Φ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ K ⍮ Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ Φ ⊳ x ↦ E )
where "Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ K ⍮ Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ Φ" := (wf_gmod Θ Ξ mp K Δ Φ) : type_scope

The filed units Θ and the stack Ξ of open frames, innermost first. A frame is checked against the frames outside it, and a unit is filed by closing the only open frame, named by its path, after which it is checked against the units filed before it. So a unit sees no stack and not itself, and a qu_rel index inside a frame counts outward from there. Freshness (frame_fresh) makes a path filed at most once.

with wf_gstack : gdeps -> gstack -> Prop :=
| wf_gstack_nil : ⊢ᵍ nil ⍮ nil
| wf_gstack_file :
  `( ⊢ᵍ Θ ⍮ (q_abs fp nil, fk_module, U) :: nil ->
     ⊢ᵍ (fp, U) :: Θ ⍮ nil )
| wf_gstack_cons :
  `( ⊢ᵍ Θ ⍮ Ξ ->
     Θ ⍮ Ξ ⍮ mp ⍮ K ⍮ Δ ⊢ᵍᵐ Φ ->
     frame_fresh Θ Ξ mp ->
     ⊢ᵍ Θ ⍮ (mp, K, gu_body Δ Φ) :: Ξ )
where "⊢ᵍ Θ ⍮ Ξ" := (wf_gstack Θ Ξ) : type_scope.

The schemes are Minimality, not Induction: nothing in this development is proved by a statement that mentions the derivation itself, and dropping the derivation arguments keeps the goals of a mutual induction readable and within reach of mauto.
A Scheme may name any subset of the block, and the judgments it leaves out survive as ordinary hypotheses in the cases that mention them.

Scheme wf_ctx_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_ctx Sort Prop
with wf_exp_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_exp Sort Prop
with wf_exp_eq_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_exp_eq Sort Prop
with wf_subtyp_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_subtyp Sort Prop
with wf_is_univ_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_is_univ Sort Prop
with wf_ext_eq_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_ext_eq Sort Prop
with wf_unit_eq_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_unit_eq Sort Prop
with wf_modexp_eq_mut_ind := Minimality for wf_modexp_eq Sort Prop.
Combined Scheme syntactic_wf_mut_ind from
  wf_ctx_mut_ind,
  wf_exp_mut_ind,
  wf_exp_eq_mut_ind,
  wf_subtyp_mut_ind,
  wf_is_univ_mut_ind,
  wf_ext_eq_mut_ind,
  wf_unit_eq_mut_ind,
  wf_modexp_eq_mut_ind.

The same with ⊢ⁿˡ: the shape of moving the judgments along a growth of the global context (gctx_embedding_preserves_wf). The flag premise of the alias, flatten and body rules asks ⊢ⁿˡ of a description, which has to move along with the rest; the fundamental theorems keep syntactic_wf_mut_ind, where it is a plain hypothesis.

with wf_exp_no_level_mind := Minimality for wf_exp Sort Prop

with wf_modexp_eq_no_level_mind := Minimality for wf_modexp_eq Sort Prop
with wf_no_level_members_no_level_mind := Minimality for wf_no_level_members Sort Prop.

The three-way scheme is the shape of wk_preserves_wf, sub_preserves_wf and sub_eq_preserves_exp: each of them transports the three judgments about a fixed context along an operation, and says nothing about context well-formedness. Generating it as a scheme in its own right (rather than combining the four-way one) means it takes exactly three predicates: the ⊢ Γ premises of rules like wf_typ survive as ordinary hypotheses.

Scheme wf_exp_mind := Minimality for wf_exp Sort Prop
with wf_exp_eq_mind := Minimality for wf_exp_eq Sort Prop
